After 2 Billion Miles, Ford Releases Mach-E Battery Report Card

TB
By Tyler Brooks Viral Concepts & Prototype Lead • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • 95% of 2021 model year Mustang Mach-Es still have a battery life above 87%, including high-mileage cars How concerned should prospective EV buyers be about battery degradation?
  • Based on a recent study that Ford conducted with its 2021 Mustang Mach-E models, it appears that the battery degradation fears of many are overblown.
  • Official reporting verified via Carscoops news desk.

95% of 2021 model year Mustang Mach-Es still have a battery life above 87%, including high-mileage cars

📌 The Core Development

How concerned should prospective EV buyers be about battery degradation? Based on a recent study that Ford conducted with its 2021 Mustang Mach-E models, it appears that the battery degradation fears of many are overblown. In fact, after analyzing more than 36,000 Mach-Es sold in the U.S. and Canada, Ford has revealed that they retained an average battery state of health of 92%.

The Mustang Mach-E first hit the market during the 2021 model year, and Ford sold more than 36,000 units that year, providing the automaker with plenty of data as to how these EVs perform in the real world. A key factor in that data is the mileage that customers have collectively racked up on their 2021 Mach-Es, which amounts to more than two billion miles driven — or more than the distance required to travel to Uranus.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Ford says that of the vehicles it has analyzed, 95% of them have batteries sitting at between 87% and 97% health. For the more than 2,000 owners who have driven their Mach-Es in excess of 100,000 miles over the past five years, the average battery health is sitting at approximately 91%. More than 30 drivers have driven their EVs over 200,000 miles, and the battery health of these vehicles averages an impressive 88%. Two owners of 2021 Mach-Es have covered more than 300,000 miles, and one of them is David Blenke , who has driven his Mach-E more than 400,000 miles on the original battery. Ford hasn't specified the battery health of his EV, simply stating it has "remained strong."

"This is one of the most valuable feedback loops we have had at this scale: more than 36,000 vehicles, five-plus years and billions of real-world miles," Technical Leader of High-Voltage Battery Cells and Systems at Ford, Kevin Vander Laan said. "Over five years, billions of miles and verified owner data give us a meaningful, real-world view of battery state-of-health over time. The data is encouraging, and the learnings continue to inform how Ford approaches battery systems, software guidance, and future electric vehicle programs."

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The Mustang Mach-E was Ford's first series EV of the modern age, designed to give the company a much-needed rival to the Tesla Model 3 and Tesla Model Y. It uses the brand's Global Electrified 1 architecture, and 2021-2022 models were sold with standard- and long-range battery packs. Evidently, these batteries can handle high mileage with minimal degradation and should certainly last the lifetime of the vehicle without needing a replacement.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Ford's next important EV is the Fathom pickup truck . This new model will start at $29,945 and be the first to use the company's Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. Its shell will be made using large aluminum castings , it will feature bidirectional charging , and use a simplified 400-volt electric architecture with the company's fifth-generation battery management system.
